topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Closer CPU
explanation: Computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to balance cost and performance.  Faster, smaller, and more expensive memory (like caches) sits closer to the CPU, while slower, larger, and cheaper memory (like main memory and disk) resides further away. Caching strategies aim to exploit locality of reference (temporal and spatial) to keep frequently accessed data in faster levels of the hierarchy, minimizing access times and improving overall system performance.
